::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Function Properties](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1495311/function-properties), asked by [opheliaxo](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/283432/opheliaxo) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-10-24; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> The question is as follows:
>
>  - Let $f$ be a function $f : U → V$ , where $U$ and $V$ are non-empty
>    sets. Prove or refute that $f$ is injective iff there is a function
>    $g : V → U$ with $g ◦ f = Id_U$ .
>
> Apparently I **cannot** assume that $g$ is injective while proving this because $U$ can be greater than $V$ which would mean that $g$ is injective. 
>
> Why can I not do this?
>
> Also, how do I then prove this? The answer given by my TA isn't clear, neither is the one given by my professor. 
>
> Thanks in advance! :)
>
> **Note: I've already received a grade on this/this is a past assignment question!**
:::

You cannot assume that $g$ is injective because that's an additional hypothesis to the statement.  It's like breaking the rules of the game.

Here is a proof: Suppose $g$ exists.
We want to show that
$$f(x) = f(y) \implies x=y$$
for all $x$ and $y$ in $U$
(this is equivalent to the definition of injective function).
Given $x$ and $y$ in $U$ with $f(x) = f(y)$, apply $g$ to both sides:
$$\begin{align*}
    g(f(x)) &= g(f(y)) \\
\implies \operatorname{Id}_U x &= \operatorname{Id}_U y \\
\implies x &= y
\end{align*}$$
So $f$ is injective.

(See if you can prove this interesting addition: $g$ must be a surjection.)

On the other hand, suppose $f$ is injective.  We have to construct $g$.  Choose an arbitrary point $u_0 \in U$.  Given $v \in V$, either $v = f(u)$ for some $u\in U$, or it isn't.  If it is, set $g(v) = u$.  If it isn't, set $g(v) = u_0$.  Since $f$ is injective, $g$ is a function (fill in the details if this isn't obvious to you). By construction, $g(f(u)) = u$ for all $u \in U$.

(Again, the $g$ constructed here must be a surjection.  Can you see why?)
